references.role: Sheet layout and fleet material style only

prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: five-view 2D orthographic reference sheet for a textured 3D reconstruction of the Stellar Syndicates CORVETTE.

Primary request: Expand the existing Corvette artwork in Image 1 into ONE polished reference sheet showing exactly five complete views of the SAME ship: FRONT, BACK, TOP, BOTTOM, SIDE.

Input roles:
Image 1 is the authoritative CORVETTE design being expanded. Preserve its distinctive silhouette, hull proportions, armor design and equipment positions.
Image 2 is the existing CRUISER reference sheet: use ONLY its presentation, restrained technical rendering, typography, background and fleet material style. Do not copy the Cruiser geometry or its engine/turret counts.

Corvette identity: compact protective escort warship. A narrow central faceted nose leads into very broad armored forward shoulders, with squared beveled outer corners and dark recessed end grilles. The hull narrows strongly aft into a reinforced central service spine. Exactly TWO modest cylindrical engine pods sit to either side of the aft spine, parallel and at the same height. A short center tail lies between the engines. Exactly FOUR small dorsal twin-barrel point-defense turrets occupy the original paired shoulder stations, two at the forward station and two just behind them. Preserve these mount positions. Put all four turrets in a neutral rest pose with their barrels parallel to the longitudinal axis and pointing toward the nose. Keep the tiny recessed forward centerline bridge, layered silver shoulder panels, dark mechanical channels, and brass collars. It has a thick armored hull, not a thin airplane wing. Keep the reference's broad forward silhouette and slimmer aft body; do not turn it into a narrow wedge or a capital ship.

Composition: wide landscape sheet, about 2:1 aspect, high native detail, clean warm-white background. TOP and BOTTOM are two large plan views side by side across the left approximately 60% of the page, noses pointing exactly UP. In the right column: FRONT above, BACK in the middle, SIDE below with its nose LEFT. Use one consistent drawing scale: TOP and BOTTOM same length and beam; SIDE same nose-to-tail length and same hull height as the end views; FRONT and BACK same width as the top-view beam. Leave clear margins, space between drawings, and a small label beneath each. Compact title at upper left. Exactly five ship drawings, no inset or additional angle.

Style and materials: clean, precise 2D colored hard-surface technical illustration like Image 2. Crisp contours and readable seams, brushed pale titanium armor, cool silver panels, gunmetal frames, restrained warm brass fasteners, tiny cyan windows, running lights and engine apertures. Subtle wear and gentle neutral shading. Fully resolved original surface textures rather than outline-only blueprints. No strong cast shadow.

Projection and consistency are essential:
TOP: straight overhead, nose UP, no pitch/yaw/perspective. Preserve Image 1's planform and four turret mounts. Engines are longitudinal housings ending in narrow edge-on nozzle rims; do not turn bright circular exhaust faces upward toward the camera.
BOTTOM: straight underneath, nose UP, identical outer silhouette, length, shoulder geometry and two engine positions to TOP. Develop a fully textured ventral hull: interlocking silver belly plates, darker central keel, flush access hatches, recessed cooling grilles, brass locks and subtle cyan service lights. Cover the full underside edge to edge. The dorsal bridge and turrets are not visible through the hull and must not be painted on the belly. Do not add landing gear, extra guns or cargo containers.
FRONT: exact level head-on orthographic elevation, camera at zero elevation on the nose axis. Fore-aft length collapses completely. Show the broad shoulders edge-on, central blunt nose cross-section, bridge rising behind it, and gun assemblies with natural occlusion of the rear pair. No overhead roof plan, long vertical nose blade, forward exhaust circles or open hangar mouths.
BACK: exact level stern-on orthographic elevation. Exactly TWO round cyan exhaust apertures, symmetrically spaced across one horizontal line, inside layered circular dark nozzle rims. A small solid centerline keel/tail between them, broad shoulder silhouette beyond. Show backs of turrets; forward-pointing gun muzzles do not face this camera. Same width and height as FRONT.
SIDE: exact level port-side orthographic profile, nose LEFT, engines RIGHT; no roof visibility or perspective. Low armored bow, bridge near the forward fifth of length, two near-side gun mounts at their distinct forward shoulder stations, barrels pointing LEFT. Far-side symmetric mounts and engine overlap the near-side ones naturally. Show one side-profile engine silhouette at the stern, on the same horizontal thrust axis, ending in an edge-on vertical nozzle rim. Do not stack engines, turn an exhaust disc toward the side camera, invent a bridge tower, or change turret stations.

All five drawings must be one physically coherent vessel: same length, beam, height, hull thickness, bridge location, four turret stations and two drive positions. Hidden surfaces are conservative continuations of the existing design. Resolve the underside as carefully as the upper hull.

Text, verbatim, exactly once each: "CORVETTE", "TOP", "BOTTOM", "FRONT", "BACK", "SIDE". Simple charcoal uppercase typography.
Avoid: extra views, perspective beauty render, separate extra ships, dimension numbers, scale specifications, grids, annotations, logos, watermark, background scenery, floor, exhaust plumes, weapons fire.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit this CORVETTE five-view concept reference sheet. Preserve TOP, BOTTOM, BACK, all six labels, the white background, materials and armor identity. Make ONLY these final consistency corrections in FRONT and SIDE.

1. FRONT (upper right): each of the two visible gun housings currently has an incorrect stack of four circular muzzle holes. Each actual turret is TWIN-BARREL. Replace each four-hole stack with exactly TWO small circular muzzle holes side by side at one height, one horizontal pair per housing, FOUR visible muzzles total. The aft pair of turrets is directly occluded by the forward pair. Do not add barrels or housings elsewhere.
The nose should be a compact closed faceted armored end face in the center. Replace the large vertical black central grille below the cyan bridge with solid silver/gunmetal frontal plating and a narrow horizontal seam. Keep the silhouette shallow. Do not expose long dorsal fuselage length in this level front view.

2. SIDE (lower right): the current bridge and guns sit too far aft, and the shoulder panel projects from the rear of the ship instead of the front. REPOSITION these parts to agree with TOP. Treat the visible profile's nose at LEFT as 0% and nozzle at RIGHT as 100%:
- Tiny low command bridge center: 21% of the nose-to-tail length.
- FIRST low gun turret center: 25% of the length, immediately behind the bridge.
- SECOND low gun turret center: 40% of the length. Two low twin-barrel turrets in profile, both barrels pointing LEFT.
- The broad thick shoulder SIDE ARMOR lies below these guns, from 18% to 49% of the length. This is the widest part of the actual Corvette. Put the large chamfered armor panel and its grille at the FRONT HALF of the profile, under both guns.
- Behind the shoulder, 49% to 77%, show the narrow central service spine as a LOW straight plated side wall, with small dark vents, subtle brass hardware and cyan service lamps. Do not use a bulky cruiser-like rear shoulder in this area.
- The cylindrical aft engine remains at 77% to 100%, lying along the horizontal thrust axis with an edge-on vertical nozzle rim at the right.
- The armored lower hull is deeper beneath the FRONT shoulder and transitions smoothly into the rear spine and engine mount.
Keep nose-left and stern-right. This must be an exact FLAT SIDE ELEVATION. Remove the broad horizontal roof planes above the shoulder and rear spine; horizontal surfaces disappear when viewed edge-on. Draw only the side armor face, upper contour, belly contour, two gun silhouettes and the low bridge. No isometric angle, second far wing, extra turret, stacked engine, end-on circular exhaust disc or tall tail.
Keep the same fine panel textures, silver titanium, dark gray structure, brass and cyan. The new side profile is a stout escort with forward shoulders and two compact rear pods as shown in the plan, not a long cruiser with mid-aft shoulders.

Everything else stays unchanged, especially the top view's FOUR twin-barrel mounts and the detailed distinct BOTTOM. Exactly five views. No extra text.

modelingNote: Concept-art reference. Use TOP as planform authority and SIDE to guide thickness; reconcile illustrated scale differences during reconstruction.
